title: Mahbub College
description: Founded in 1862 at Secunderabad as the Anglo Vernacular School, later renamed Mahbub College for the sixth Nizam, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan.
dedication: In memory of the Asaf Jahi dynasty
subtitle: Secunderabad · Founded 1862

items.value: For the sixth Nizam, Mir Mahbub Ali Khan

blocks.intro: Mahbub College at Secunderabad began in 1862 as the Anglo Vernacular School, founded by Somasundaram Mudaliar. It was later renamed in honour of the young sovereign Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, the sixth Nizam, whose patronage supported the school's growth. Set up as a Western-style English-medium school for the sons of the state's officers and the British residency establishment at Secunderabad, it became, with its elegant colonnaded main block — still in use — one of the earliest institutions of Hyderabad to teach the modern sciences and English literature alongside Persian and Arabic, setting a model that the later Asafi schools and colleges of the city would follow.

sections.eyebrow: A School Renamed for a Nizam
sections.title_html: From Anglo Vernacular School to Mahbub College
sections.sub: A Secunderabad school that took the sixth Nizam's name
body: The school that became Mahbub College was founded in 1862 by Somasundaram Mudaliar as the Anglo Vernacular School. It was renamed for Mir Mahbub Ali Khan, the sixth Nizam, whose support helped establish it among the most prestigious English-medium schools in the state — part of the same era of educational expansion that, under Salar Jung I's reforming administration from 1853 onward, also produced City College, the engineering and survey schools, and the modern courts of Hyderabad State.<cite data-ref="karen-leonard-1978"></cite>

sections.sub: A colonnaded Anglo-Indian block and broad playing fields
body: The school occupies an extensive site at Secunderabad, with a colonnaded principal block in the late nineteenth-century Anglo-Indian institutional manner, a chapel-like assembly hall, and broad playing fields. The buildings have been added to repeatedly, but the original frontage remains.

sections.sub: Educator of Hyderabad's civil and military officers
body: Mahbub College has educated several generations of Hyderabad's civil and military officers, and remains a leading school of the twin cities. It is now Mahbub College High School, affiliated to the state board, and continues on its original campus.<cite data-ref="wikipedia-mahbub-college"></cite>

references.text: Karen Leonard, Social History of an Indian Caste: The Kayasths of Hyderabad, University of California Press, 1978.
